_meta.indication: DIFICID is a macrolide antibacterial drug indicated in adults (≥18 years of age) for treatment of Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled noninferiority trial comparing 10 days fidaxomicin 200 mg po bid to vancomycin 125 mg po qid; enrolled US and Canadian subjects
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) confirmed by >3 unformed bowel movements in the 24 hours prior to randomization and a positive toxin assay
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical cure at the end-of-treatment (EOT) visit (Day 10-11)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure at EOT: fidaxomicin 88% vs vancomycin 86%, difference 3% (95% CI -2.9%, 8.0%) — noninferiority met. Global Cure: fidaxomicin 70% vs vancomycin 57%, difference 12.7% (95% CI 4.4%, 20.9%) — superiority.

nct_ctgov.title: Fidaxomicin Versus Vancomycin for the Treatment of Clostridium Difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD) (MK-5119-018)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled noninferiority trial comparing 10 days fidaxomicin 200 mg po bid to vancomycin 125 mg po qid; enrolled subjects in Canada, the US, and Europe
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) confirmed by >3 unformed bowel movements in the 24 hours prior to randomization and a positive toxin assay
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical cure at the end-of-treatment (EOT) visit (Day 10-11)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure at EOT: fidaxomicin 88% vs vancomycin 87%, difference 1% (95% CI -4.8%, 6.8%) — noninferiority met. Global Cure: fidaxomicin 72% vs vancomycin 57%, difference 14.6% (95% CI 5.8%, 23.3%) — superiority.

nct_ctgov.title: PAR-101/OPT-80 Versus Vancomycin for the Treatment of Clostridium Difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions: nausea (11%), vomiting (7%), abdominal pain (6%), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (4%), anemia (2%), and neutropenia (2%).
target_moa: Fidaxomicin is a macrolide antibacterial that is bactericidal against C. difficile in vitro, acting by inhibition of bacterial RNA polymerase (RNA synthesis).

advisory_committee.vote: Anti-Infective Drugs' Advisory Committee on April 5, 2011 voted unanimously that the applicant had demonstrated the efficacy and safety of fidaxomicin for the treatment of CDAD.

description.text: Expanded CDAD treatment indication to include pediatric patients from 6 months to less than 18 years of age

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA expands the approved indication for the treatment of *Clostridioides difficile*-associated diarrhea (CDAD) in adults to include pediatric patients from 6 months to less than 18 years of age and provides updates to sections of the prescribing information (PI) relevant to the use of fidaxomicin in pediatric patients from 6 months to less than 18 years of age.

basis.text: In October 2003 fidaxomicin was granted fast track designation for treatment of CDAD based on its potential to avoid the side effects of currently accepted treatments and/or prevent relapses of CDAD.

citations.quote: In October 2003 Fidaxomicin was granted fast track designation for treatment of *Clostridium difficile*- Associated Diarrhea (CDAD) by the Division of Anti-Infective Drug Products. The designation was based on fidaxomicin's potential to avoid the side effects of currently accepted treatments and/or prevent relapses of CDAD.

basis.text: Based on results showing superiority of fidaxomicin to vancomycin in sustained clinical response, the NDA was granted priority review status.

summary.text: Fidaxomicin received fast track designation in October 2003 for CDAD, and the NDA was granted priority review based on superiority to vancomycin in sustained clinical response; it was approved first cycle under a standard (non-accelerated) pathway following a unanimous favorable Anti-Infective Drugs' Advisory Committee vote.

citations.quote: In October 2003 Fidaxomicin was granted fast track designation for treatment of *Clostridium difficile*- Associated Diarrhea (CDAD) by the Division of Anti-Infective Drug Products.
Based on results showing superiority of fidaxomicin to vancomycin in sustained clinical response, the NDA was granted priority review status.
The committee voted unanimously that the applicant had demonstrated the efficacy and safety of fidaxomicin for the treatment of CDAD.

requirement.text: 1757-001: Conduct a prospective clinical trial of 10 days of fidaxomicin in at least 32 pediatric patients (6 months to less than 18 years of age) with C. difficile-associated diarrhea to evaluate safety and pharmacokinetics (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: **1757-001:** Conduct a prospective clinical trial of 10 days of Difcicid (fidaxomicin) in at least 32 pediatric patients (6 months to less than 18 years of age) with *C. difficile*-associated diarrhea to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics (including serum and fecal concentrations) of Difcicid (fidaxomicin).

requirement.text: 1757-002: Conduct a prospective, randomized clinical trial to demonstrate safety and effectiveness of fidaxomicin compared to vancomycin in pediatric patients (6 months to less than 18 years of age) with C. difficile-associated diarrhea (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: **1757-002:** Conduct a prospective, randomized clinical trial to demonstrate safety and effectiveness of Difcicid (fidaxomicin) compared to vancomycin in pediatric patients (6 months to less than 18 years of age) with *C. difficile*-associated diarrhea.

requirement.text: 1757-003: Conduct a prospective study over a five-year period after introduction of fidaxomicin to the market to determine if decreased susceptibility to fidaxomicin is occurring in C. difficile (required under 505(o)).
